visuals.title: Which path is Alt Standard #24?
visuals.prompt: Select the QC path that uses the ACR Digital Mammography QC Manual as FDA's approved alternative for FFDM/DBT.

feedback.a: That is the default (e)(6) manufacturer path, not Alt #24.
feedback.b: Correct. Alt Standard #24 points to the ACR DMQC Manual path.
feedback.c: The dose ceiling applies to both paths; it is not itself Alt #24.

visuals.explanation: FDA Alt #24 allows ACR DMQC (+ DBT Supplement) with the ACR phantom as an alternative to manufacturer QC; the 3.0 mGy ceiling remains.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Regions described by position; labels revealed after answering. SCHEMATIC — NOT A MAMMOGRAM.

visuals.title: Where is the initial power-drive maximum band?
visuals.prompt: Select the segment that represents the 111–200 N initial power-drive maximum force band.

feedback.a: That marks the minimum available force, not the max-drive band.
feedback.b: Correct. Initial power-drive maximum must be between 111 and 200 N.
feedback.c: Above 200 N exceeds the allowed initial power-drive maximum.

visuals.explanation: Federal compression device performance sets ≥111 N available and 111–200 N initial power-drive maximum.

visuals.title: Which step is the time-out?
visuals.prompt: Select the Universal Protocol step that occurs just before the procedure starts.

feedback.a: Verification comes earlier and includes consent review.
feedback.b: Site marking is the middle step.
feedback.c: Correct. Time-out is the final pause just before the procedure.

visuals.explanation: Universal Protocol: verification, site marking, then time-out immediately before the procedure.

glossary.definition: FDA-approved alternative allowing FFDM/DBT facilities to follow the ACR Digital Mammography QC Manual (and DBT Supplement) with the ACR Digital Mammography Phantom instead of manufacturer QC, while still obeying the 3.0 mGy phantom dose ceiling.
Laterally exaggerated craniocaudal mammography view (also glossed as cranio-caudal exaggerated to the axilla).
Mammography view in which the breast is rolled to one side.
Wrong-site/wrong-procedure/wrong-person prevention framework summarized by AHRQ as preprocedure verification, site marking, and time-out.
Final preprocedure pause immediately before an invasive procedure to confirm correct patient, procedure, and site/side.
